column18: The condition reads ONLY stmt->kind, a bounded AstKind enum value.  No helper call, no cc-> read, no host graph write, no pointer identity operation, no callback, no recovery state.  The enclosing function parseDefaultStatement does own the host AST list, but the CANDIDATE SUB-DECISION does not.

Already PolyC-owned.  The live C decision body is compiled out of the production object.  The CALL SITE projects stmt->kind and stmt->declvar->kind with the original && short-circuit and passes them to the PolyC component.

column15: The dispatch DECISION is separable from the 12 statement constructors it calls.  The decision maps ONE bounded token pair (tok->tk_type, tok->i64) onto ONE bounded statement-constructor SELECTOR; the CALL of the selected constructor, the host AST construction, the token cursor advance, the recovery state and the diagnostics all stay on the C side of the seam.  This is EXACTLY the shape of the two already-migrated decisions: parseSwitchArmTerminates(int kind) and parseCompoundBlockAppendsStatement(int,int) are pure scalar functions whose CALL SITES retain every host ownership.  For SUB-004 the equivalent factoring is a pure keyword -> statement-selector classifier; the 12 constructors are the dispatch TARGETS, chosen by the decision and invoked by the C host.
column18: The dispatch reads tok->tk_type (an enum) and tok->i64 (a bounded keyword id), and selects among 12 statement CONSTRUCTOR callbacks.  The 12 callbacks are the DISPATCH TARGETS, not calls made BY the decision: the decision returns one of them.  The projection of the decision itself is the bounded token pair.  The host AST, the token cursor, the recovery state and the diagnostics all stay on the C side of the seam.

TRANSITIVELY DEPENDS on the mutable cc->symbol_table, cc->clsdefs and cc->uniondefs.  The chain is: parseDeclOrStatement calls cctrlIsKeyword(cc,tok->start,tok->len); cctrlIsKeyword (src/cctrl.c:1306) calls cctrlGetKeyWord(cc,name,len); cctrlGetKeyWord (src/cctrl.c:1290) reads mapGetLen(cc->symbol_table,name,len), then mapGetLen(cc->clsdefs,name,len), then mapGetLen(cc->uniondefs,name,len).  All three are MUTABLE host maps.  PROVEN MECHANICALLY: DEPENDS mode reports DETECTOR=MUTABLE_HOST_STATE_DEPENDENCE with DEPENDENCE_SITE=TRANSITIVE_THROUGH_A_CALLEE.  The projection is therefore NOT bounded.

The compound statement body loop.  It reads and writes the host AST body list (listAppend(body->stms,stmt)), restores cc->current_recovery = outer_recovery, and drives the token cursor.  It REQUIRES nonlocal recovery and performs host graph writes.

column1: # THE SUB-005 TRANSITIVE MUTABLE-HOST-STATE DEPENDENCE, PROVEN
# The claim "SUB-005's projection does not depend on the mutable symbol
# table" is FALSE, and it is PROVEN MECHANICALLY against the live
# POSITIVE BASELINE (a candidate that genuinely has no dependence):
# THE SOURCE-BOUND TRANSITIVE CHAIN (every hop quoted from the live
# source, with its file and line):
#      -> the candidate calls cctrlIsKeyword with the cc POINTER.
#      -> the cc POINTER is passed through unchanged.
#      -> THREE MUTABLE HOST MAPS are read: cc->symbol_table,
# All three maps are MUTATED during parsing (mapAdd on cc->symbol_table
# on every declaration, on the class definitions and on the union
# definitions).  The projection is therefore a function of unbounded,
# mutable host state, and SUB-005 is INELIGIBLE until that dependence
# is eliminated or bounded and proven.  It is NOT eliminated here.
# SUB-004's range CONTAINS the 12 statement-constructor calls, and a
# naive reading would count 12 parser callbacks.  That would be
# WRONG, for a reason that is now stated precisely:

#         parseSwitchStatement retains the token cursor, the recovery
#         state, the AST construction and the diagnostics.  The
#         migrated function itself has ZERO callbacks and ZERO host
#         state.  Its ABI is `I64 ast_kind -> I64 terminate`.
#      -> the same shape.  The call site at 2177 performs the
